mainTopic: The seller's extra weight (הכרעה and גירומין), and רבי לוי's teachings on false measures, theft and blessings
overview: The משנה teaches that a seller must tilt the scale a טפח in the buyer's favor. If he weighed exactly, he must add extra amounts (גירומין). Local custom also decides how goods are measured. The גמרא first brings ריש לקיש's source, ״וצדק״, for the tilting. It then concludes that tilting is only local custom, and that ריש לקיש's פסוק really teaches the גירומין. רב gives the liquid rate as a tenth of a ליטרא per ten ליטרין, and the dry-goods rate stays a תיקו. Then come teachings of רבי לוי. Cheating with measures is harsher than עריות because it cannot be fixed through תשובה. Robbing a person is worse than robbing הקדש. ה׳ blessed ישראל with twenty-two letters and cursed with only eight, while משה רבינו did the opposite.

steps.title: The seller tilts the scale; if he weighed exactly, he adds extra
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the seller must tilt the scale a טפח for the buyer. If he weighed exactly, he must add גירומין: one in ten for liquids and one in twenty for dry goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the seller must tilt the scale a handbreadth for the buyer. If he weighed exactly, he gives extra amounts: one in ten for liquids, and one in twenty for dry goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה, continuing from earlier, tells us the seller must give the buyer a little more than the exact weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to give the buyer extra. The first is to tilt the scale a טפח toward the buyer. The second applies if the scale was balanced exactly: then the seller must add a fixed extra amount, which differs for liquids and dry goods.

keyTerms.meaning: To tilt the scale (so it leans toward the buyer's side)
Extra amounts added to the weight

phrases.english: And he is obligated to tilt [the scale] for him a handbreadth.
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the seller, carried over from the earlier part of the משנה.

phrases.english: If he was weighing for him exactly,
phrases.notes: Literally 'eye to eye': the two pans hang perfectly even.

phrases.english: he gives him extra amounts.
one for ten with liquids,
and one for twenty with dry goods.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller tilts the scale a טפח. If he weighed exactly, he adds גירומין: 1/10 for liquids, 1/20 for dry goods.

steps.title: Measuring must follow local custom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that local custom decides whether to measure with small or large vessels, and whether to level off or heap up the measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where people usually measure with a small vessel, one may not use a large one, and where they use a large one, one may not use a small one. Where they level the top, one may not heap it, and where they heap it, one may not level it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to measuring by volume. It says the seller must follow the local custom and may not switch methods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small versus large vessels, and leveled versus heaped measures, can change how much the buyer actually gets. Changing the method on your own breaks the fair understanding between buyer and seller.

keyTerms.meaning: To level off the top of the measure
To heap up above the rim

phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed to measure with a small [measure] –
one may not measure with a large one.
With a large one – one may not measure with a small one.
To level – one may not heap.
To heap – one may not level.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring follows local custom: small or large vessels, leveled or heaped.

steps.title: Where does the tilting rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that the seller must tilt the scale.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for a source for the משנה's rule. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the tilting rule needs a source, maybe even from the Torah. This assumption is what the גמרא will test and change in the next few steps.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn these things?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters [derived]?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first rule, tilting the scale a טפח.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the obligation to tilt the scale (הכרעה).

steps.title: ריש לקיש: "Be righteous with your own"
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the source is ״אבן שלמה וצדק״, read as "make it just from your own and give it to him."
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says "a perfect and just weight." This means: be generous from what is yours and give it to the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question with a פסוק. He reads the word צדק as a command to the seller to give a little extra from his own goods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of the פסוק is about honest weights. ריש לקיש reads צֶדֶק as צַדֵּק, an instruction to go beyond exact. At this point the גמרא connects this to the tilting rule, which would make tilting a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Be righteous (generous) from what is yours

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said,
for the verse says: "A perfect and just weight" –
phrases.notes: דברים 25:15

phrases.english: be just from your own and give to him.
phrases.notes: He reads צֶדֶק (justice) as צַדֵּק, a command: be generous.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tilting comes from ״וצדק״: be generous from your own and give to the buyer.

steps.title: If tilting is a Torah law, how can he weigh exactly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the סיפא allows weighing exactly and adding גירומין. If tilting were a Torah law, weighing exactly should not be allowed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the later part of the משנה: if he weighed exactly, he gives extra amounts. But if tilting is from the Torah, how can he weigh exactly in the first place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that tilting the scale is a Torah law, using the later part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא treats exact weighing as a normal option that only needs extra added afterward. A Torah law requiring tilting would not let the seller skip it. So tilting cannot be a Torah requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
If he was weighing for him exactly –
he gives him extra amounts.
But if tilting is from the Torah,
how can he give him exactly?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 4) that tilting is learned from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא allows exact weighing. That fits only if tilting is not a Torah obligation.

steps.title: Tilting is only local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רישא, requiring tilting, speaks of a place where that is the custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first part of the משנה is talking about a place where people are used to tilting the scale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem. It says tilting the scale is not a Torah rule but a local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the רישא and סיפא fit together. Where the custom is to tilt, the seller tilts. Where it is not, he may weigh exactly and add גירומין. This raises the question of what ריש לקיש's פסוק was about, which the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
In a place where it is the custom

phrases.english: Rather, the first clause is in a place where they are accustomed;
phrases.notes: Meaning the custom there is to tilt the scale a טפח.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the רישא applies only where that is the custom.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tilting is a Torah obligation everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tilting is only a local custom, so exact weighing with גירומין is allowed elsewhere.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's פסוק moves to the גירומין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that if ריש לקיש's statement was said at all, it was said about the סיפא, the obligation to add גירומין, learned from ״וצדק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if ריש לקיש's statement was said, it was said about the later part: if he weighed exactly, he gives extra amounts. From where do we know this? ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says "and just." Be generous from your own and give to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps ריש לקיש's teaching but moves it to the rule of adding גירומין after exact weighing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק and the same reading come back, but now they support a different rule. The required Torah generosity is the גירומין, not the tilting. That is why the גמרא repeats the whole statement.

keyTerms.meaning: On the later part (of the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Tilting the scale is only custom. The Torah source ״וצדק״ (ריש לקיש) supports the obligation to give גירומין when weighing exactly.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is repeating itself for no reason. The same ריש לקיש statement now supports a different rule: the גירומין, not the tilting.

phrases.english: And if [the statement] of Reish Lakish was said –
it was said on the latter clause:
If he was weighing for him exactly –
he gives him extra amounts.
From where are these matters [derived]?
Reish Lakish said, for the verse says: "And just" –
be just from your own and give to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַסֵּיפָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by moving ריש לקיש's derivation from the רישא to the סיפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The obligation to give גירומין after exact weighing is learned from ״וצדק״.

steps.title: How much are the extra amounts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact size of the גירומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much are the extra amounts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the amount of גירומין. It is setting up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said "one for ten" for liquids, but it is not clear what that ratio is measured against. The גמרא wants it spelled out.

phrases.english: And how much are the extra amounts?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact amount of the גירומין.

steps.title: רב: a tenth of a ליטרא per ten ליטרין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל quotes רב: for liquids, the extra is one tenth of a ליטרא for every ten ליטרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said in the name of רב: for liquids, one tenth of a ליטרא for every ten ליטרין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the משנה's "one for ten" for liquids as a tenth of a ליטרא added for every ten ליטרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the extra is much smaller than a tenth of the whole sale. A tenth of a ליטרא on ten ליטרין comes to one part in a hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: A ליטרא, a unit of weight

steps.whatToRemember: For liquids, the גירומין are a tenth of a ליטרא per ten ליטרין, which is one part in a hundred.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said that Rav said:
one tenth of a litra for liquids –
for every ten litra.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל אָמַר רַב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For liquids: one tenth of a ליטרא per ten ליטרין (1/100).

steps.title: How should the משנה's numbers be read?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about adding one for ten with liquids and one for twenty with dry goods. It asks whether the dry rate is one twentieth of a ליטרא per twenty, or one tenth of a ליטרא per twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one for ten with liquid, and one for twenty with dry. They asked: what does it mean? Is it one tenth per ten of liquid and one twentieth per twenty of dry? Or is it one tenth (of a ליטרא), both for ten of liquid and for twenty of dry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's numbers and asks what exactly they mean for dry goods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings agree about liquids: a tenth of a ליטרא extra for every ten ליטרין, just like רב said in Step 9. The question is only about dry goods. Is it a twentieth of a ליטרא for every twenty ליטרין (a smaller extra), or a tenth of a ליטרא for every twenty ליטרין (a bigger extra)?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)

phrases.english: One for ten with liquid,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. It is the extra amount the seller adds on top of the exact weight.

phrases.english: and one for twenty with dry, etc.
A question was raised before them:
How is he saying it?
One tenth with liquid, for ten of liquid,
and one twentieth with dry, for twenty of dry;
or perhaps,
one tenth, for ten of liquid
phrases.notes: In this reading, the same one tenth of a ליטרא is used for both kinds of goods.

phrases.english: and for twenty of dry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב gave the liquid rate, the גמרא asks how the משנה's dry rate should be read.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dry-goods extra one twentieth of a ליטרא per twenty ליטרין, or one tenth of a ליטרא per twenty ליטרין?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not find an answer, so it leaves the question unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means there is no proof either way. The exact dry-goods extra stays an open question, and this closes the discussion about the size of the גירומין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question stays unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: Liquids get a tenth of a ליטרא extra per ten ליטרין. For dry goods, it is unresolved whether the extra per twenty ליטרין is a twentieth or a tenth of a ליטרא.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question of Step 10 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about the dry-goods rate is left unresolved.

steps.title: False measures are punished more harshly than עריות
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says the punishment for false measures is harsher than for עריות. By עריות the Torah uses the short word אל, and by measures it uses the longer word אלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: the punishment for measures is harsher than the punishment for עריות. For these (עריות) the word אל is said, and for those (measures) the word אלה is said.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רבי לוי says that cheating with measures is punished more harshly than עריות, and he points to two Torah words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words mean 'these'. By עריות the Torah uses the short form אל, and by false measures it uses the fuller form אלה. רבי לוי reads the fuller form as a sign of a harsher punishment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
Harsher is the punishment of measures
than the punishment of forbidden relationships,
for with these (עריות), "el" is said,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:27, where the word appears as הָאֵל.

phrases.english: and with those (measures), "elleh" is said.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:16, right after the פסוקים about honest weights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: קָשֶׁה עוֹנְשָׁן שֶׁל מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how serious it is to cheat with measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment for false measures is harsher than the punishment for עריות.

steps.title: How do we know אל means harshness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that the word אל points to something harsh.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we see that this word אל means harshness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי לוי for his source that the word אל means 'harsh'. It is setting up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי's whole argument depends on these words showing how severe something is. So the גמרא first asks for proof that אל carries a meaning of harshness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can it be shown

phrases.english: And from where is it shown
that this "el" means harsh?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי אֵל קָשֶׁה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רבי לוי's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the word אל means harshness or strength.

steps.title: Proof from "the mighty of the land"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in יחזקאל where אילי means the strong, mighty people of the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And the mighty of the land he took."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that uses a related word to mean 'mighty'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אילי, 'the mighty ones', comes from the same root as אל. That shows the word carries a sense of strength and harshness. This supports רבי לוי's reading of the two words.

keyTerms.meaning: The mighty ones of the land

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the mighty of the land he took."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 17:13

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In יחזקאל, the related word אילי means 'mighty', so אל carries a meaning of harshness.

steps.title: But עריות also has the word אלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי לוי: the Torah also uses אלה by עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: By עריות too, isn't אלה written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי לוי: the 'strong' word אלה also shows up by עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי said measures are harsher because only they get the word אלה. If עריות also has אלה, then his difference between the two falls apart.

phrases.english: Regarding forbidden relationships also,
isn't "elleh" written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of רבי לוי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי לוי's claim that only measures get the harsher word אלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word אלה also appears by עריות, so it cannot mark measures as harsher.

steps.title: The אלה by עריות comes to leave out measures from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the אלה by עריות has a different job. It teaches that measures do not carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to exclude measures from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the אלה by עריות is not there to show harshness. It is there to teach a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By עריות, אלה means 'these', and only these, get כרת. That leaves out cheating with measures, so it has no כרת. The word is used for a limit, not to show severity.

keyTerms.meaning: The punishment of being cut off

steps.confusionAlert: This answer saves the word-reading, but it creates a new problem: if measures have no כרת, how can they be 'harsher'? The next step asks exactly that.

phrases.english: That one
comes to exclude measures from כרת.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אלה by עריות shows that עריות are also very harsh.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אלה by עריות limits כרת to עריות and leaves out measures.

steps.title: Then what makes measures harsher?
steps.stepSummary: Since measures have no כרת, the גמרא asks what extra severity they have.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is their extra severity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if measures don't even get כרת, in what way are they harsher than עריות? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that עריות carry כרת and measures do not. That seems to make עריות more severe, so רבי לוי's claim now needs a different explanation.

phrases.english: But then what is their extra severity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in Step 16, which seemed to make עריות more severe.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי לוי's claim that measures are punished more harshly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עריות carry כרת and measures do not, so where is the greater harshness of measures?

steps.title: Measures are harsher because תשובה is not possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that for עריות a person can do תשובה, but for false measures he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, תשובה is possible; here, תשובה is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra harshness of measures is that the sinner cannot fix it through תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harshness is not about the kind of punishment. It is about whether the sin can be undone. The usual explanation is that someone who cheated many customers cannot know whom to pay back, so his תשובה cannot be complete.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי לוי: false measures are harsher than עריות. Not because of כרת, which measures lack, but because cheating with measures cannot be fully fixed through תשובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how serious a sin is can depend on whether it can be repaired, and not only on how big its punishment is.

phrases.english: That there, it is possible through repentance,
phrases.notes: 'There' means עריות; 'here' in the next line means false measures.

phrases.english: and here, it is not possible through repentance.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָתָם אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְשׁוּבָה, וְהָכָא לָא אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 and backs up רבי לוי's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the severity to a different area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Severity is measured by the punishment, so עריות, which carry כרת, would be harsher.
steps.terutzMaskana: Measures are harsher because the sin cannot be fixed through תשובה.

steps.title: Robbing a person is worse than robbing הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that גזל הדיוט is more severe than גזל גבוה, because the פסוק about robbing a person mentions חטא before מעילה, while the פסוק about הקדש mentions מעילה before חטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי לוי said: Stealing from an ordinary person is more serious than stealing from הקדש. In the case of stealing from a person, the פסוק puts the word 'sin' before 'מעילה'. In the case of הקדש, the פסוק puts 'מעילה' before 'sin'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי לוי, comparing stealing from a person with stealing from הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים in ויקרא use the same two words, חטא and מעילה, but in opposite order. The פסוק about cheating a person opens with 'sin', while the פסוק about הקדש opens with 'מעילה'. רבי לוי reads this order as showing that hurting a fellow person is the more serious sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Stealing from 'the Most High', meaning taking הקדש property
Misusing הקדש property; also used for betrayal or breach of trust

steps.whyThisMatters: This continues רבי לוי's theme from the previous steps: sins that hurt other people, like false measures and theft, are treated as especially severe.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi says:

phrases.aramaic: קָשֶׁה גֶּזֶל הֶדְיוֹט יוֹתֵר מִגֶּזֶל גָּבוֹהַּ,
phrases.english: Robbing an ordinary person is more severe than robbing the Most High,
phrases.notes: 'Robbing the Most High' means taking property that belongs to הקדש.

phrases.english: for with this one, the verse puts 'sin' before 'me'ila',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21, about cheating a neighbor.

phrases.english: and with that one, it puts 'me'ila' before 'sin'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:15, about misusing הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: קָשֶׁה גֶּזֶל הֶדְיוֹט יוֹתֵר מִגֶּזֶל גָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of רבי לוי's teaching on false measures, the גמרא brings another related teaching of his about sins against people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Robbing a person is more severe than misusing הקדש, as shown by the word order of the פסוקים.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא blessed with twenty-two and cursed with eight
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי opens a new teaching: the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא is unlike the way of people. He blessed ישראל with twenty-two and cursed them with only eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי לוי said: Come and see that the way of people is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. הקדוש ברוך הוא blessed ישראל with twenty-two, and cursed them with only eight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי states a new idea in short form. The next steps will explain what 'twenty-two' and 'eight' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that ה׳'s blessing is much bigger than His curse. The numbers are not explained yet, so this step sets up the explanation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see, an opening phrase that introduces a lesson
The way of 'flesh and blood', meaning human beings
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi says: Come and see,
that unlike the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the attribute of flesh and blood.

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא – בֵּרַךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, blessed the Jewish people with twenty-two,
and cursed them with eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה, שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching of רבי לוי, joined to the previous ones because they share the same author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s blessing of ישראל was much larger than His curse: twenty-two compared with eight.

steps.title: Explaining the twenty-two and the eight letters
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that the numbers are letters of the alphabet. The blessings in בחקתי run from 'אם' (א) to 'קוממיות' (ת), all twenty-two letters. The curses run from 'ואם' (ו) to 'נפשם' (ם), only eight letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He blessed them with twenty-two: from 'אם בחקתי' until 'קוממיות'. He cursed them with eight: from 'ואם בחקתי תמאסו' until 'ואת חקתי געלה נפשם'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי explains his numbers by pointing to the first and last words of the blessings and of the curses in פרשת בחקתי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessings begin with א and end with ת, so they cover the whole alphabet. The curses begin with ו and end with ם, and from ו to מ is only eight letters. So the blessing is 'complete', while the curse is only partial.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you walk in My statutes', the opening of the blessings (ויקרא 26:3)
'Upright', the last word of the blessings (ויקרא 26:13)
'And if you reject My statutes', the opening of the curses (ויקרא 26:15)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Twenty-two' and 'eight' are not counts of blessings and curses. They are counts of alphabet letters, from the first letter of the section to its last letter.

phrases.english: He blessed them with twenty-two:
from 'If you walk in My statutes' until 'upright';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:3 to 26:13. It starts with א and ends with ת, so it covers the whole alphabet.

phrases.english: and He cursed them with eight:
from 'And if you shall reject My statutes'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:15, which starts with the letter ו.

phrases.english: until 'And My statutes were abhorred by their soul'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:43, which ends with ם. Counting from ו through מ gives eight letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּרְכָן בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם – מֵ״אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי״ עַד ״קוֹמְמִיּוּת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the numbers twenty-two and eight that רבי לוי stated in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessings in בחקתי span the whole alphabet (א to ת), while the curses span only ו to מ, eight letters.

steps.title: משה רבינו did the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי contrasts this with משה רבינו, who blessed ישראל with eight letters and cursed them with twenty-two. The גמרא begins to explain the eight, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But משה רבינו blessed them with eight and cursed them with twenty-two. He blessed them with eight:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי now gives the 'flesh and blood' side of the comparison: משה רבינו did the reverse. The last words begin an explanation that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the contrast promised in step 20: ה׳'s blessing is larger than His curse, while משה's curse is larger than his blessing. The source for משה's eight-letter blessing is about to be given.

phrases.english: And yet Moses, our teacher,
blessed them with eight,
and cursed them with twenty-two.
He blessed them with eight:
phrases.notes: The source for this comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ – בֵּרְכָן בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה, וְקִלְּלָן בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the human side of the contrast that רבי לוי introduced in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה רבינו, a human being, blessed with only eight letters and cursed with twenty-two, the opposite of ה׳.
